title: SpaceX Market Value Drops More Than $400B in Less Than a Month

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Shares of SpaceX declined more than 5% on Thursday, hitting their lowest trading level since August. The daily drop capped a period of steep valuation losses for the company, which has seen more than $400B of its market value erased in less than 30 days.

The market reaction follows the release of third-quarter results detailing a shift in capital spending toward the company's artificial intelligence infrastructure. SpaceX directed 84% of its quarterly capex toward AI, expanding its computing capacity to 1.7 GW. This investment has weighed on other segments; the space launch business reported a $7M operating loss compared to a $259M profit a year ago. Meanwhile, the Starlink connectivity business generated 85% of total operating profit for the period, though average monthly revenue per consumer subscriber fell to $69 from $83.

selectedTweets.text:
SpaceX Q3 2026 results: key takeaways by segment.  

Super Intelligence:

• Swung from a $1.7B operating loss to $431M of operating income, after $1.2B of stock-based pay tied to the Cursor acquisition.
• Cursor, acquired in mid-August, added $608M of revenue.
• Computing capacity reached 1.7 GW, nearly triple a year earlier, as SpaceX builds out Colossus II.
• Most AI revenue now comes from cloud services and infrastructure: $7.0B, against $538M from advertising.
• AI capex more than tripled from a year ago.

Connectivity:

• Consumer subscribers nearly doubled, to 13.6M.
• Monthly revenue per user fell from $83 to $69.
• Enterprise and government sales grew 91%.

Space:

• Launch business went from a $259M operating profit a year ago to a $7M loss.
• 35 launches, down from 44, while R&D spending rose 44% as Starship development stepped up.
